messages:
Carla: Quick status check — where are we on the token-cost attribution schema? I thought schema PRs were split into event + mapping, want to make sure owners are set before we cut the canary.
Sam: Mapping PR is merged (thanks @Jia for the review), event schema PR is still open with the final enum changes. link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/instr/pulls/482
Jia: I left one comment about the lat_bucket naming, otherwise ready. I can approve once we standardize the field (low/med/high vs numeric cutoffs).
Carla: Ok — who owns the final decision on cutoff values? Need that for the telemetry dashboard folks.
Mark: I can own the cutoff decision. I'll sync with SRE on realistic lat buckets (p99 thresholds vary by model). Will post numbers by EOD.
Lee: Heads up — model inference team needs the mapping for token attribution to land before we flip the new cost calc in prod. If mapping lands but event schema delayed we can backfill for a week but prefer not.
Sam: Noted. Plan: merge mapping into prod branch today, hold event schema until Carla + Mark signoff, then create canary pipeline.
Carla: Sounds good. @TelemetryBot can you schedule a canary rollout for Thursday 11:00 PST with 5% traffic to dedicated stacks?
TelemetryBot: Scheduled canary: 2026-03-19 11:00 PST, 5% traffic to redwood-dedicated-canary. Notifying infra on-call.
Jia: Infra dependency: the new event schema requires a small change to event-ingest lambda env var (MAX_EVENT_SIZE). I have a PR but need eng-infra to approve infra infra/PR#211
Sam: @Jia thanks — pinging @Mark for infra approval since he said he'd own cutoffs and can coordinate with infra.
Mark: Ack. I'll review infra/PR#211 now. If it's just var bump we'll approve and tag for canary.
Lee: Quick CR queue update: I have 3 open reviews (mapping tests, e2e for attribution, and a tiny perf tweak). Prioritize the e2e so we can validate end-to-end before canary.
Carla: Priorities: 1) event schema signoff, 2) infra var merge, 3) e2e tests merged. Assign owners: Mark (cutoffs + infra), Jia (event schema PR followups), Lee (e2e and perf).
Sam: I'll prepare the canary playbook and a rollback script. Will post runbook link: https://confluence/redwood/canary/instr-canary-playbook
Jia: Two quick Qs — do we want the latency breakdown field to be a nested object or flattened prefixed fields? Nested breaks current ingestion parsers.
Carla: Flattened prefixed fields for now (lat_ms_p50, lat_ms_p95, lat_ms_p99). We can revisit after a short migration window.
Lee: For the attribution mapping, I found a corner case where cached responses double-count tokens when prefix caching and reranking both apply. Adding a small dedupe step in the mapper. Will include test.
Sam: Good catch. If you can add test and PR today, we still keep schedule.
Mark: Cutoff numbers: proposing p50<80ms, p95<300ms, p99<900ms for baseline models. Posting details and rationale here: https://docs.redwood/cutoffs/2026-03-18.md
Carla: Thanks Mark — that's enough to finalize event schema enum and mapping thresholds. Jia, please reflect that in the schema PR.
Jia: Will do. Expect updated PR in ~2 hours.
TelemetryBot: Reminder: next telemetry sync meeting is 2026-03-20 16:00 UTC. Agenda: schema rollout, canary metrics, post-canary backfill plan.
Lee: One more ask — who will monitor token-cost regression during canary? We need someone to watch per-route unit cost and token attribution counts.
Sam: I'll own the initial monitoring dashboard during the canary window. Lee, if you can own the regression alert thresholds we can collaborate on playbook.
Lee: Got it. I'll add alert rules to the dashboard (token_cost_increase_percent > 10% over baseline triggers paging).
Carla: Great. If no major blockers after Jia's update we'll merge event schema and kick the canary tomorrow. Thanks all — post updates as PRs land. :thumbsup:
